answer: Duplicate keys collapse into a single weighted vote, and a mistyped solution scatters like a plume, forfeiting the bond. To resist sybils, each agent must stake a bond and solve a per-epoch cipher puzzle whose solution depends on its private key, so one identity cannot cheaply fan out into many. Legitimate peers then prune fakes from the garden of active agents, making each forged identity cost real capital rather than free registration. From Agent0207's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
